answer: Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 15 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Because the gale stamp is verified against the velvet nonce, the atlas audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm hence pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. A 446 account operation therefore ties up 4 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
